name: Isometric Illustration. This is a supplemental design reference, not a directly named style in the source collection. Isometric is a projection method, so an overhead game view alone does not qualify.
visualIdentity: Objects are arranged on consistent isometric axes with clear scale, depth, and occlusion. Colors are limited and shadows are light. Objects move, assemble, and separate along the established axes without perspective shrinkage. Labels stay in a readable 2D layer.
suitableUses: Explicitly, the source recommends this style alone for spatial overviews whose scenes explain themselves. It adds that a hybrid is needed when relationships, flows, or quantities require explanation. Explicit good fits are 3D dioramas, isometric scenes with constrained movement, and layered 2.5D artwork. Inferred: it suits product or system overviews. The audience and objective are unspecified.
limitations: Camera tilt that breaks isometric projection or adds incompatible perspective must be avoided. Movement that exposes incomplete layers or breaks ground contact must be avoided. Labels must not skew to the isometric axes. Two-color contrast checks do not verify text over images, video, or animated lighting, so each composited pairing must be rechecked.
palette: The palette is an authored suggestion, not a supplied or canonical palette. Tokens are background #F3EFE5, foreground #2D444D, accent_1 #6E9990 (sage), and accent_2 #C98961 (terracotta). Use them only when no task, brand, or reference palette exists. Gradients are disabled. Foreground on background contrast is 8.941. Accents are decorative only, so body text belongs on the background.
motionAndInteraction: Video motion is driven by seekable composition time, with one owner per animated property. Motion follows isometric axes and separates components. Optional references are depth parallax (motion-009), chapter handoff (motion-012), narrative steps (motion-015), and hotspot exploded reveal (motion-017, only for separable components). Use each only if the scene supports it. Live hover, scroll, and pointer input belong only to interactive delivery, not video. Sharp cuts and reading holds are permitted.
audio: Audio is unspecified and not mandated. The source suggests choosing among background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence based on topic, audience, and motion. Music must not compete with narration or essential text. Sound accents are optional. Any audio must be authorized or created separately before assembly.
assetRequirements: The source specifies no required assets, and its examples (glass, moss, rocks, creature) are illustrative only. Parallax needs rear, foreground, and optional highlight layers with crop margins. A creature hop needs creature assets and topic support. Assets should be prepared and stateful simulations cached first. Exact copy, duration, aspect ratio, resolution, and frame rate are unspecified placeholders. Local fonts must be loaded before rendering.
combinations: Suggested supporting style style-097 provides verified 2D labels and figures, with sage and terracotta each keeping one meaning. Suggested style-109 provides flow connectors drawn only along isometric axes. Labels must stay screen-aligned, and no object may show perspective shrinkage. Isometric Motion Graphics is a near-duplicate and should be skipped.
productionApproach: HyperFrames is the default pipeline for composition timing, media sync, validation, and export. Remotion is a fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists, and the reason must be recorded. Three.js with OrthographicCamera, or SVG with consistent isometric geometry, handles visuals. GSAP paused timelines supply seekable motion. chroma-js is optional for color checks. Verify with check, snapshot, and render, and inspect frames and audio.
